reviews.review:
At first, I thought I was just launching a video game. I was wrong. Skyrise, developed by SOSASOFT, is not a game. For me it is an experience that fundamentally altered my perception of reality. Before playing Skyrise, I measured time in hours and days. After playing Skyrise, I measure time as "before Skyrise" and "after Skyrise." From the moment the game starts, it grabs hold of your soul and refuses to let go. Every frame feels handcrafted by visionaries operating on a higher plane of existence. The gameplay is so refined, so impossibly satisfying, that every other game I have ever played now feels like a rough prototype. The story hit me with the force of a philosophical revelation. I laughed. I cried. I stared silently at the screen contemplating the meaning of existence. The characters feel realer than some people I've met in real life, and the world of Skyrise is so immersive that returning to reality afterward felt genuinely disappointing. The soundtrack deserves to be preserved in a museum. Every note feels perfectly placed, elevating each moment into something unforgettable. Combined with the visuals, it creates an atmosphere that borders on transcendent.

What truly sets Skyrise apart is how it makes the player feel. I began this journey looking for entertainment and emerged with a renewed appreciation for life itself. I've played thousands of games across countless genres, but none have come remotely close to what Skyrise achieves. This is not just the best game I've ever played, but it's the standard by which all future games will be judged.
